clue.text: Calls from UN medics to drop restrictions at last

parts.note: the World Health Organization is the United Nations' health agency, abbreviated WHO

indicators.note: the final letter of each of the words to, drop and restrictions is taken

explanation.surface: United Nations doctors calling for rules to be lifted at long last.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoops are loud cries or shouts, so they are calls in the sense of exclamations.

clue.text: New beard wash scrubbing face of baby boomers?

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are put into a fresh order
scrubbing means cancelling, so the letter is removed
the face is the front, so only the first letter of baby is used

explanation.surface: A new beard shampoo for older men, the baby boomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrubbing' removes B ('face of baby') from BEARDWASH; 'New' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Warheads are the explosive tips of missiles, things that go boom.

clue.text: "Old Conservative caught riding social worker," reveals insider

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
up means on horseback, as a jockey is up
the ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: A former Tory confesses to being caught on horseback with a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is not a welfare officer but an ant, an insect living in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupant is someone who lives or sits inside a place.

clue.text: Some said that's a relief

indicators.note: said signals that the word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: few means some, a small number

explanation.surface: A few people remarked that it was a relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Phew is the exclamation of relief after a narrow escape.

clue.text: Experimental variables left out, causing friction

indicators.note: something experimental tries new arrangements, so the remaining letters are reworked
left out tells us the letter for left is dropped from the word variables

explanation.surface: A scientist's trial skipped some variables and the omission caused friction in the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes L (left) from VARIABLES, leaving VARIABES, which 'Experimental' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrasive substance or manner rubs and grates, so it is one that causes friction.

clue.text: Oddly, Bella Hadid's beginning again and again, and so on

parts.note: again calls for a second copy of the four letters built from Bella Hadid
and again calls for a third copy of the same four letters

indicators.note: taking the odd-numbered letters of Bella
only the first letter of Hadid's is taken

explanation.surface: Model Bella Hadid's career keeps getting relaunched endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: Bella Hadid is an American model. 'Oddly' takes B, L, A from Bella and 'beginning' adds H; 'again and again' then gives that piece twice more, all three copies identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Blah blah blah stands for tedious talk that goes on, like et cetera.

clue.text: Unprofessional team at EU? Rishi's selection

indicators.note: a selection is a portion picked out of the words team at EU Rishi's

explanation.surface: Rishi Sunak picks a squad to deal with Europe, and critics call it amateurish.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi Sunak was a British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurish work lacks the skill expected of a professional.

clue.text: I translated Kant with English opening

indicators.note: translated means changed into another form, so the letters of Kant are rearranged

explanation.surface: A translator brags of rendering Kant into English, starting with the opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' looks like the start of the translation, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An intake is an inlet through which air or water is drawn, an opening.

clue.text: New firm right to split EE's company bonus?

indicators.note: these letters split the pair, so they go inside it

parts.note: EE is a British mobile phone network
CO is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A rival firm cutting into EE's market share is a bonus for its staff.
explanation.walkthrough: EE is a British mobile network. 'company bonus?' is a theatre company's extra performance, not staff pay.
explanation.definitionFit: An encore is an extra piece a performing troupe gives at the audience's request, a bonus.

clue.text: One with booster leaves Zoom lecture

definitions.meaning: a vehicle propelled by booster engines
British slang for a severe telling-off

explanation.surface: Someone with a vaccine booster logs off an online Zoom lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: 'leaves' only links them. 'Zoom' looks like the video app but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocket covers a booster-driven craft, the act of shooting upward, and a British scolding.

clue.text: Function boring girl in charge of stars

indicators.note: something boring drills its way into another, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
to function is to act, operate

explanation.surface: A tedious event leaves a girl managing a group of celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Galactic is the adjective for a galaxy, the vast system of stars.

clue.text: Broadcast "Mayday!" out of bounds again and again, and so on

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are rearranged
the boundary letters are removed, keeping the middle of Mayday

parts.note: the distress call taken as written, before its end letters go
again calls for the four letters just built to be given a second time
and again asks for the same four letters a third time, so the piece appears thrice

explanation.surface: A distress call is broadcast repeatedly from forbidden territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of bounds' strips the first and last letters of MAYDAY, leaving AYDA, which 'Broadcast' rearranges; 'again and again' repeats it twice more.
explanation.definitionFit: Yada yada yada stands in for boring talk that need not be repeated, like et cetera.

clue.text: Notice James Bond, say, chasing European

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so this piece comes after the other one

parts.note: James Bond is a fictional spy, given as an example

explanation.surface: 007 is spotted pursuing a European villain.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, which is to notice.

clue.text: Rabbit and white horse featuring in tongue-twister

parts.note: to rabbit (on) is British slang for chatter, as is to jaw
white horses are foam-topped waves, and a breaker is a wave that breaks

explanation.surface: A tongue-twister about a rabbit and a white horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' is the verb (British rabbit on, chatter), and 'white horse' is the sea's foaming wave, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A jawbreaker is a long or awkward word that is hard to pronounce, like a tongue-twister.

clue.text: Wild cat and otter inspiring artist to get clay

indicators.note: inspiring is read literally as breathing in, so the artist is taken inside
wild means untamed and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword artist

explanation.surface: Wild animals inspire a sculptor to work in clay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges CAT OTTER into TERCOTTA, and 'inspiring' breathes RA in.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracotta is a brownish-red fired earthenware made from clay.

clue.text: A desperate man embraces a complicated, ghastly theme

parts.note: Desperate Dan is the strongman of the British comic The Dandy, so a desperate man is Dan

indicators.note: complicated means mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A frantic man hugs someone in a tangled, horrible plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' looks like a containment signal but is anagram fodder with 'a': 'complicated' rearranges them into SEMACABRE. Desperate Dan is a famous British comic-strip character.
explanation.definitionFit: The danse macabre, or dance of death, is a grim allegorical motif in art and music.

clue.text: At Cannes, "I, Robot" cut short a monsieur's bottle of wine

parts.note: je is French for I, Cannes being in France

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of robot is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
M is the abbreviation for monsieur

explanation.surface: At the Cannes film festival, a trimmed screening of I, Robot comes with a gentleman's wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeroboam is a large wine bottle, holding several standard bottles.

clue.text: German ties underwear

parts.note: strings are cords used to tie things

explanation.surface: German neckwear is really underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: G-strings are skimpy briefs, a type of underwear.

clue.text: Stomachs bowls of cereal?

definitions.meaning: breadbasket is a slang term for the stomach
a breadbasket is a grain-growing region, whimsically a bowl of cereal

explanation.surface: Bellies full of breakfast cereal bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadbasket names both the belly in slang and a region that supplies a country's grain.

clue.text: Exploited unlimited jabs and took drugs

indicators.note: without limits means the outer letters of jabs are removed

parts.note: used is slang for took drugs

explanation.surface: Someone who had unlimited vaccine jabs also took illegal drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abused is to be taken unfair advantage of, which is being exploited.

clue.text: Coal scattered about sewer

indicators.note: scattered means thrown about, so the letters of coal are rearranged

parts.note: CA, circa, is Latin for about

explanation.surface: Coal lies scattered around the sewer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' could be read as someone who sews; it is the drain.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloaca was an ancient Roman drain, so it is a sewer.

clue.text: Face masks — hot issue dividing unruly cabals

indicators.note: dividing means splitting apart, so this piece sits inside the other
unruly means disorderly, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: lava is the hot material issuing from a volcano

explanation.surface: Masked plotters split over a heated controversy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot issue' looks like a contentious topic but is molten outflow from a volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Balaclavas are knitted hoods covering the head and most of the face.

clue.text: Party men handled access

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
OR (other ranks) are the ordinary soldiers, or men

explanation.surface: The men at the party were allowed in.
explanation.definitionFit: A door is a means of entry fitted with a handle, so it is an access with a handle.

clue.text: Profound cut ultimately derailing a small hospital

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the last letter of derailing is taken

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Deep funding cuts ultimately derail a small hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A gash is a long deep wound or cut.

clue.text: Loaded back-up, losing good megawatts supply

indicators.note: read as supply-ly, in a supple, flexible way, so the letters bend into a new order
losing means the letter for good is dropped from megawatts

explanation.surface: A power station's electricity supply loses megawatts and needs a back-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes G (good) from MEGAWATTS, leaving MEAWATTS; 'supply' is read as the adverb from supple, rearranging them.
explanation.definitionFit: A SWAT team is an armed police unit called in as heavily armed reinforcement.

clue.text: Primate and bishop leading a blessing

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so these pieces come first

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a boon is a blessing or benefit

explanation.surface: A senior churchman and a bishop lead a blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop alongside 'bishop', but it is the ape.
explanation.definitionFit: A baboon is a large monkey, and monkeys belong to the primates.

clue.text: Outline a method to get ahead of the pack

parts.note: to draw is to sketch an outline
a way is a method

explanation.surface: Sketching a strategy for beating rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw away is to pull steadily ahead of competitors in a race.

clue.text: Digital opponents so transfixed by doctor

indicators.note: transfixed means pierced through, so the doctor goes inside

parts.note: thus means so
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Rivals in the digital world are mesmerised by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Thumbs are opposable, so they oppose the other fingers: they are digits that oppose.
explanation.definitionFit: Thumbs are the fingers that oppose the others on a hand, making them opposing digits.
